interconnect_topology_options: Point-to-point Interconnection (Chapter 1.4 / 8.9 / Figure 1-7) — one MASTER + one SLAVE; simplest scheme.
Shared Bus Interconnection (Chapter 8.10 / Figure 1-8 / Figure 1-9) — one common bus with arbitration; multiplexor-based OR three-state-based variants permitted by the spec.
Crossbar Switch Interconnection (Chapter 1.7 / Figure 1-4) — parallel channels between multiple MASTERs and multiple SLAVEs; aggregate throughput by parallel operation.
Data Flow Interconnection (Chapter 1.7 / Figure 1-5) — IP cores arranged in a pipelined sequential flow, each core with both SLAVE input and MASTER output; concurrency through pipeline parallelism.

Off-Chip Interconnection (Glossary / Figure 1-6) — Wishbone interface extends off-chip via standard I/O pads (although the spec notes Wishbone is optimized for on-chip and off-chip use will generally operate at slower speeds — 1.2 Objectives).

interconnect_role.INTERCON: WISHBONE module that interconnects MASTER and SLAVE interfaces. Routes CLK_O -> all CLK_I, RST_O -> all RST_I, and connects MASTER outputs to SLAVE inputs (and vice versa) via the chosen topology. May also implement arbitration, partial address decoding, watchdog timers (RECOMMENDATION 3.10), and termination injection.
interconnect_role.SYSCON: Generates [CLK_O] (system clock) and [RST_O] (system reset). Distributed to all WISHBONE interfaces via INTERCON. SUGGESTION 3.00 — SYSCON should assert [RST_O] during power-up, hold it until voltages and clocks stabilize, then negate it synchronously.

interconnect_rules: MASTER and SLAVE signal naming is canonically MASTER-prefixed (e.g. [ADR_O()]); in point-to-point and many other topologies the corresponding SLAVE signal differs (e.g. [ADR_I()]); RULE 2.20 — signal names MUST adhere to the rules of the native tool used.
SYSCON connects [CLK_O] to every [CLK_I] and [RST_O] to every [RST_I]. RULE 3.00 / RULE 3.15 enforce the reset behaviour.
Standard mode: SLAVE [ACK_O] / [ERR_O] / [RTY_O] generated from the logical AND of [CYC_I] AND [STB_I] (RULE 3.35).
Pipelined mode: master is throttled by SLAVE [STALL_I]; up to N outstanding requests before N matching [ACK_I] pulses arrive (Section 3.1.3.2).
If multiple MASTERs share a SLAVE through an arbiter, the arbiter MAY use [CYC_O] / [LOCK_O] to grant ownership; once granted, the SLAVE serves a single MASTER until ownership is released.
RECOMMENDATION 3.10 — INTERCON SHOULD include a watchdog that monitors MASTER [STB_O] and asserts [ERR_I] / [RTY_I] if a cycle exceeds the time limit; misbehaving interfaces MAY be disconnected.
RECOMMENDATION 3.15 — registered MASTER outputs on [STB_O] and [CYC_O] to keep them off the critical path.

User-defined tags ([TGA_O()], [TGD_O()], [TGD_I()], [TGC_O()], [TGC_I()]) are propagated through the INTERCON if the topology supports them (point-to-point trivially; crossbar/shared-bus by integrator design).
fields.default_signal_values_when_omitted: Optional signals omitted from an IP core's interface are tied off at the integration boundary: [ERR_O], [RTY_O] tied LOW if not implemented (their absence means the SLAVE can only normally terminate); [LOCK_O] tied LOW if not implemented (cycles are interruptible); [CTI_O] tied to 3'b000 (Classic) if not implemented by either side (Section 4.3 / RULE 4.10); [BTE_O] tied to 2'b00 (Linear) if incrementing bursts are not used; [SEL_O] tied to all-1s if granularity = port size (entire bus is selected).

slave_classification.general_slave: Decodes [ADR_I()] using full or partial decoding (Section 8.10.4); asserts [ACK_O] on logical AND of [CYC_I] and [STB_I] from the address-matched range.
slave_classification.memory_slave: Wishbone-mapped memory (RAM/ROM) — Section 8.7. FASM Synchronous RAM/ROM Model (Section 8.7.1) uses [ACK_O] to qualify read data; supports SINGLE / BLOCK cycles.
slave_classification.fifo_slave: Section 2.2.3 OBSERVATION — [ADR_O()] array may not be present on the interface for FIFOs.
slave_classification.register_slave: I/O register block; uses [SEL_O()] to support byte / halfword / word writes to the same register.
slave_classification.dual_port_slave: Section 2.2.3 OBSERVATION — [CYC_O] is useful for interfaces with multi-port interfaces (such as dual-port memories) because it requests use of a common bus from an arbiter.
slave_classification.bridge_slave: AHB-to-WB, AXI-to-WB, PCI-to-WB and similar bridges — appear as a SLAVE on the WISHBONE side and a MASTER on the other-protocol side. May use [RTY_O] to indicate temporary unavailability.

interface_categories: SLAVE interface (responds to transfers; drives [DAT_O], [ACK_O], [ERR_O], [RTY_O], [STALL_O], [TAGN_O]; consumes [ADR_I], [DAT_I], [SEL_I], [WE_I], [CYC_I], [STB_I], [TAGN_I])
INTERCON (interconnects MASTER and SLAVE interfaces; not a separate signal set — may be implemented as point-to-point wires, shared bus with arbiter+mux+decoder, crossbar, or data-flow chain)
fields.register_slice_insertion_rule: Wishbone does not have a formal AXI-style register-slice spec. Pipelined mode (Section 3.1.3.2) inherently allows registered SLAVE responses without breaking the cycle (at the cost of one wait state per transfer — OBSERVATION 3.50). For deeper pipelining or off-chip extension, Chapter 4 Registered Feedback bus cycles use [CTI_O] / [BTE_O] tags to advertise the cycle type so the SLAVE can prepare a registered response in advance (avoids the wait state).
fields.wishbone_to_other_bridge_summary: Wishbone-to-other-bus bridges are common (e.g. WB-to-AHB, WB-to-AXI, WB-to-APB, WB-to-PCI). The Wishbone side appears as either a MASTER (for upstream-initiated transfers) or a SLAVE (for downstream peripherals) depending on direction. Error/retry mappings are bridge-specific and outside the Wishbone spec.

address_decoding_options.Full_Address_Decoding: Each SLAVE decodes all available address bits. Used by standard microcomputer buses (PCI, VMEbus). Implies more redundant logic.
address_decoding_options.Partial_Address_Decoding: Each SLAVE decodes only the bits it requires for its decode window. Used by SoC interconnects. Less redundant logic, supports variable address sizing, and is the WISHBONE preferred approach (Section 8.10.4).

arbitration_methodology.user_defined: The arbitration methodology is defined by the end user (1.1 Features). Common choices: priority arbiter, round-robin arbiter.
arbitration_methodology.arbitration_via_CYC: Arbitration logic often uses [CYC_I] to select between MASTER interfaces (OBSERVATION on page 28). Keeping [CYC_O] asserted indefinitely may lead to arbitration problems (RECOMMENDATION 3.05).
arbitration_methodology.lock: [LOCK_O] used by MASTER to request complete ownership across multiple bus cycles; INTERCON does not grant the bus to any other MASTER until [LOCK_O] or [CYC_O] is negated.

evidence.quote: Variable core interconnection methods support point-to-point, shared bus, crossbar switch, and switched fabric interconnections. Multiprocessing (multi-MASTER) capabilities. Arbitration methodology is defined by the end user (priority arbiter, round-robin arbiter, etc.). Supports various IP core interconnection means, including: Point-to-point, Shared bus, Crossbar switch, Data flow interconnection, Off chip.

Crossbar switches are mechanisms that allow modules which are connected to communicate. Each connection channel can be operated in parallel to other connection channels. This increases the data transfer rate of the entire system by employing parallelism. Crossbar interconnections are also scalable.

An interconnection where data flows through a prearranged set of IP cores in a sequential order. Data flow architectures often have the advantage of parallelism, whereby two or more functions are executed at the same time.

CLK_O: The system clock output [CLK_O] is generated by the SYSCON module. It coordinates all activities for the internal logic within the WISHBONE interconnect. The INTERCON module connects the [CLK_O] output to the [CLK_I] input on MASTER and SLAVE interfaces. RST_O: The reset output [RST_O] is generated by the SYSCON module. It forces all WISHBONE interfaces to restart.

WISHBONE supports both full and partial address decoding. Full decoding is the method used by standard microcomputer buses (PCI, VMEbus). Partial decoding is preferred for SoC because it uses less redundant logic and supports variable address sizing.
